title: Matplotlib Labels, Titles, Ticks and Legends
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and main concepts of Matplotlib Labels, Titles, Ticks and Legends.
Create a Matplotlib Figure and Axes suitable for the visualization task.
Apply the relevant plotting API and configure its key properties.
Inspect plotted artists or chart properties to verify the intended result.
Choose labels and visual encodings that communicate data accurately.
prerequisites: NumPy arrays and basic numeric data

understand.concept: Titles and axis labels explain the subject and units of a chart. Tick locations and labels define the scale shown to the reader. Legends identify multiple series. Labels should be accurate, concise and consistent with the data.
understand.whyItMatters: A chart without context can be misunderstood even when its plotted values are correct.
understand.analogy: A map needs a title, scale and key; a chart needs a title, axes and legend.
understand.summary: Matplotlib Labels, Titles, Ticks and Legends is part of the Matplotlib learning path. The examples use deterministic data and the Agg backend for automated execution.

explain.narrative: Read the concept, execute each example in sequence, inspect the printed result and compare it with the expected output. Each example creates a figure with the non-interactive Agg backend and closes it after inspection.

examples.title: Set title and axis labels
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.set_title('Weekly orders'); ax.set_xlabel('Week'); ax.set_ylabel('Orders')
print(ax.get_title(), ax.get_xlabel(), ax.get_ylabel())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The three labels describe the chart and both dimensions.

examples.title: Create a legend
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2], [3, 4], label='Actual')
ax.legend()
print(ax.get_legend().get_texts()[0].get_text())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The legend uses the line label.

examples.title: Set x-axis limits
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.set_xlim(0, 5)
print(tuple(ax.get_xlim()))
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Limits define the visible axis interval.

examples.title: Set explicit tick positions
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.set_xticks([0, 1, 2])
print(ax.get_xticks().tolist())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Ticks mark selected positions on an axis.

examples.title: Provide custom tick labels
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.set_xticks([1, 2]); ax.set_xticklabels(['Jan', 'Feb'])
print([t.get_text() for t in ax.get_xticklabels()])
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Custom labels translate numeric positions into meaningful categories.

practise.guidedTask: Create a small program demonstrating matplotlib labels, titles, ticks and legends. Use a deterministic dataset, configure the relevant chart properties, and print at least one check that verifies the result.
practise.independentTask: Apply the technique to a small dataset of your own. Include meaningful labels, check input lengths and explain why the chosen chart is appropriate.
hints: Start with a small deterministic dataset.
Create the Figure and Axes explicitly with plt.subplots().
Inspect the relevant artist or Axes property instead of relying on visual output alone.
Add labels and units that accurately describe the data.
Close figures after automated checks or file export.
practise.challenge: Build a reusable plotting function that validates its inputs, creates the requested chart, and returns or saves a well-labelled Figure without leaking open figures.
validationCriteria: All five examples execute under the pinned Python and Matplotlib environment and match expected output.
